intended_object: The index n − 1 in `Fin n`, i.e. the last coordinate, used to name the standard basis vector e_{n−1}, which represents the "vector" class of the discriminant group of the checkerboard lattice D_n. Inferred from the docstring.
explanation:
The definition builds `⟨n - 1, _⟩ : Fin n` under `[NeZero n]`. That is exactly what its docstring says: the last element of `Fin n`. It is correct.

It is not a mathematical object in its own right, though. It is a small indexing helper that picks out one coordinate so the library can write down a representative of the vector class of the D_n discriminant group. That coordinate choice is a convention: any index would give a representative of the same class.

The same element already exists in Mathlib. It is the top element `⊤` of `Fin n` under `Fin.instBoundedOrder [NeZero n]`, and it can also be reached through `Fin.last` up to the identification `n = (n - 1) + 1`. Since this is a convenience definition and not a mathematical notion, the verdict is not_a_mathematical_object.
